channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Nicotine’s Terrifying Little Secret
item.description: The most “terrifying” thing about nicotine may be how poorly it is understood. Public fear often focuses on nicotine itself, while the far greater danger comes from inhaling smoke produced by combustion. That misunderstanding has consequences: smokers may avoid lower-risk alternatives because they believe nicotine is the main cause of smoking-related disease. Better public health communication should separate dependence from harm, and fear from evidence. (Published on July 30, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: Is Cash Corrupting the Philippines?
item.description: Follow the money, and tobacco policy often starts to look less like public health and more like power management. In the Philippines, questions around funding, influence and regulation raise a deeper concern: who gets to shape the rules, and whose interests are protected when safer nicotine products are restricted. Public health decisions should be transparent, evidence-based and insulated from financial pressure. When cash enters the room, scrutiny should enter with it. (Published on July 30, 2026byplanetofthevapes.co.uk)

item.title: Burnham's Britain stops following the science and starts following the vibez
item.description: When policy starts following the “vibez”, evidence is usually the first thing pushed aside. Britain’s approach to nicotine increasingly risks being shaped by mood, optics and moral signalling rather than by comparative risk. That matters because smokers make decisions in the real world, not inside campaign slogans. If science says smoke-free alternatives are not the same as cigarettes, public policy should not pretend otherwise. (Published on July 31, 2026bydaily-pouch.com)
